content: Vytorin is a medication that combines two active ingredients, ezetimibe and simvastatin, to lower cholesterol levels. It is available in tablet form in four different strengths: Vytorin 10/10 (10 mg ezetimibe / 10 mg simvastatin) Vytorin 10/20 (10 mg ezetimibe / 20 mg simvastatin) Vytorin 10/40 (10 mg ezetimibe / 40 mg simvastatin) Vytorin 10/80 (10 mg ezetimibe / 80 mg simvastatin). This medication is used to reduce total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol (commonly referred to as bad cholesterol), and triglycerides (fatty substances in the blood). Additionally, it helps increase HDL cholesterol (known as good cholesterol). Vytorin is prescribed for patients who cannot adequately control their cholesterol levels through diet alone. It is important to continue following a cholesterol-lowering diet while taking this medication. Vytorin works in two ways: it reduces the absorption of cholesterol in the digestive tract and decreases the cholesterol produced by the body itself. However, it is not intended for weight loss. Who should not take Vytorin? You should not take Vytorin if: You are allergic to ezetimibe, simvastatin, or any of the inactive ingredients in the medication. You have active liver disease or abnormal liver function tests indicating potential liver problems. You are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Vytorin is not recommended for children under 10 years of age. What should I tell my doctor before and while taking Vytorin? Inform your doctor immediately if you experience unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness. Rarely, muscle problems can become severe, leading to muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis) and kidney damage. The risk of muscle breakdown is higher at higher doses of Vytorin and in patients with kidney problems. Certain substances can increase the risk of muscle problems when taken with Vytorin. It is crucial to inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following: Cyclosporine Danazol Antifungal agents (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole) Fibrates (e.g., gemfibrozil, bezafibrate, fenofibrate) Antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin) HIV protease inhibitors (e.g., indinavir, nelfinavir, ritonavir, saquinavir) Nefazodone (an antidepressant) Amiodarone (used for irregular heartbeats) Verapamil (used for high blood pressure or heart conditions) Large doses of niacin (≥1 g/day) Large quantities of grapefruit juice (more than 1 quart daily). Additionally, inform your doctor if you are taking coumarin anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin) or any other prescription, over-the-counter, herbal, or natural remedies. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions, including any history of liver problems or significant alcohol consumption. Vytorin may not be suitable for you in these cases. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, do not take Vytorin. If you become pregnant while on this medication, stop taking it immediately and contact your doctor. Similarly, do not use Vytorin if you are breastfeeding. Inform any other healthcare providers prescribing new medications that you are taking Vytorin. How should I take Vytorin? Your doctor will determine the appropriate dose of Vytorin for you. The available doses are 10/10, 10/20, 10/40, and 10/80. The usual starting dose is Vytorin 10/20. Take Vytorin once daily in the evening, with or without food. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, do not take an extra dose. Simply resume your usual schedule. Continue adhering to a cholesterol-lowering diet while taking Vytorin. Consult your doctor if you need dietary guidance. Do not stop taking Vytorin unless instructed by your doctor. Stopping the medication may cause your cholesterol levels to rise again. What should I do in case of an overdose? Contact your doctor immediately if you suspect an overdose. What are the possible side effects of Vytorin? Regular check-ups with your doctor are necessary to monitor your cholesterol levels and detect any side effects. Blood tests may be performed to assess liver function before starting Vytorin and during treatment. Common side effects reported in clinical studies include headache and muscle pain. Rare but serious side effects include: Allergic reactions, such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, which may cause difficulty breathing or swallowing (seek immediate medical attention if this occurs). Rash or hives. Joint pain. Muscle pain. Abnormal blood test results. Liver problems (sometimes severe). Pancreatitis (inflammation of the pancreas). Nausea. Dizziness. Tingling sensations. Depression. Gallstones or gallbladder inflammation. Report any of these or other medical issues to your doctor while taking Vytorin. This is not a complete list of side effects; consult your doctor or pharmacist for a comprehensive list. What should I know about high cholesterol? Cholesterol is a type of fat found in your blood. It is produced by your body and also comes from the food you eat. Total cholesterol consists of LDL (bad cholesterol) and HDL (good cholesterol). LDL cholesterol can accumulate in the walls of your arteries, forming plaque. Over time, this plaque buildup can narrow the arteries, reducing or blocking blood flow to vital organs like the heart and brain. High LDL cholesterol is a major risk factor for heart disease and stroke. HDL cholesterol helps prevent the buildup of LDL cholesterol in the arteries. Triglycerides are another type of fat found in the body that can contribute to health problems. General information about Vytorin Medications are sometimes prescribed for conditions not mentioned in patient information leaflets. Do not use Vytorin for conditions other than those for which it was prescribed. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. This summary provides the most important information about Vytorin. For more details, consult your doctor or pharmacist. You can also request information written for healthcare professionals. Inactive ingredients in Vytorin Vytorin contains the following inactive ingredients: butylated hydroxyanisole NF, citric acid monohydrate USP, croscarmellose sodium NF, hydroxypropyl methylcellulose USP, lactose monohydrate NF, magnesium stearate NF, microcrystalline cellulose NF, and propyl gallate NF.
